subject: Rapid failover: brief summary and next steps for Meadow Health
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@meadowhealth.com>, Meadow Health SRE <sre@meadowhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rapid failover: brief summary and next steps for Meadow Health

Hi Elena / Meadow SRE team,

Wanted to reach out with an immediate summary and next steps after the automated routing failover that affected some hosted-generation requests for Meadow Health between 06:48 and 07:05 PT this morning.

What happened (short):
- At 06:48 PT an internal routing controller hit a misclassification of GPU pool health and initiated a rapid multi-pool failover for a subset of requests routed to your region.
- The failover caused short-lived duplication and elevated latencies for ~2.1% of your generation requests; a small fraction saw 5xx retries before the system converged.

Impact to you:
- Elevated p95 latency from ~420ms to ~1.9s for affected requests; token cost unchanged.
- Retry/replay behavior produced a small spike in duplicate completions for calls with no-idempotency guard (~0.03% of tokens).

What we did:
- Disabled the faulty controller rule at 06:52 PT and executed a targeted rollback at 06:58 PT.
- Enabled short-term request deduplication at the edge to suppress obvious duplicates.
- Kicked off ops bridge and confirmed routing convergence by 07:05 PT.

Immediate ask from you:
- Can you confirm if you saw any customer-facing errors or duplicate outputs you want us to suppress or reverse?

Attachments: timeline + ops logs attached.

I will follow up with a consolidated post-incident summary once we complete the initial root-cause analysis. Apologies for the disruption — we know you depend on predictable latency.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270430-failover-timeline.pdf (timeline, annotated), ops-bridge-log-excerpt.txt (relevant bridge excerpts)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@meadowhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meadow Health SRE <sre@meadowhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 07:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid failover: brief summary and next steps for Meadow Health

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick note.

We did see a handful of strange completions in our production logs and one customer reported garbled follow-up content around 06:55 PT. I'm attaching our internal trace ids separately to the SRE alias.

Two asks from us:
1) Please share the list of request ids (or a time-bound query) so we can correlate on our side.
2) Any guidance on whether to expect token-level duplication billing adjustments?

We can set up a short bridge if helpful.

— Elena
Head of Platform Reliability
Meadow Health
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Meadow Health SRE <sre@meadowhealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@meadowhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rapid failover: brief summary and next steps for Meadow Health

Elena — thanks for the quick note.

Short answers:
- We'll produce a bounded list of request IDs (and a query string) for the 06:45–07:10 PT window and share within the hour.
- Billing: we will not charge duplicate completions generated by our transient retry amplification; we will coordinate an internal credit and share a statement you can attach to your accounting team.

Operational details we will include in the follow-up:
- Exact time slices of the misclassification signal and the rule change that triggered cascade failovers.
- Per-pool error/latency graphs and an initial hypothesis that the controller mis-evaluated a transient GPU IO metric spike as a hard failure.

Bridge: we can do a quick 30-min sync at 09:15 PT if that works for your team — Ben and Marissa will be on the call for ops detail.

— Olga
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: internal: post-incident actions and owners (Meadow Health)

Internal notes only — not for external distribution.

Summary of immediate actions (owners):
- (Ben) Run diff on routing-controller rule versions and produce exact commit that rolled at 06:48 PT. Deliverable: commit id + short rationale (ETA 10:00 PT).
- (Marissa) Aggregate per-pool p95/p99 graphs and attach pre/post snapshots to postmortem doc; include sample request ids (ETA 09:45 PT).
- (Sean) Prepare billing adjustment statement and draft credit line for duplicate completions; sync with finance (ETA 11:30 PT).
- (Olga) Share request-id export and ops-bridge log excerpts with Meadow (ETA 08:30 PT).

Keep this tight — we want the external summary to land by 11:00 PT.
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@meadowhealth.com>, Meadow Health SRE <sre@meadowhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps — Meadow Health failover

Hi Elena — quick follow-up with the items we discussed on the bridge earlier.

1) Request ID export: attached is a CSV-friendly subset and a time-bound query you can run against our logs. (See ops-bridge-log-excerpt.txt for correlated events.)
2) Short RCA (initial): controller rule misclassification caused a premature failover when a transient GPU IO metric briefly exceeded the safety threshold. The rule evaluation window was too narrow for this metric, amplifying a short spike into a failover decision.
3) Mitigations in flight:
   - We widened the evaluation window for the IO metric and toggled the controller to conservative mode; this prevents single-spike failovers (deployed 09:02 PT).
   - We added a short debounce before multi-pool failover decisions (deployed 09:20 PT).
   - Edge deduplication will remain on for 48 hours to reduce customer-visible duplicates.
4) Billing: Sean will send a formal credit statement; duplicates during the 06:48–07:05 PT window will be credited.

Next steps:
- Formal postmortem doc (internal + redacted external summary) will be published to the link below by EOD tomorrow.
- We will coordinate a short retro with your SREs next week to validate the mitigation and any additional hardening you want.

Link to status page incident: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2027-04-30-rapid-failover
Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/incident-20270430-postmortem

If you want anything more urgent before the full postmortem, call my cell or ping the SRE alias.

— Olga
